references.text: Psalm 103:22 describes God's work as a continuous activity in which all his creatures are called to praise him, reflecting Jesus' point that the Father is constantly working.
In Psalm 139:17-18, the psalmist emphasizes that God's thoughts and deeds are infinite and enduring, a theme that resonates with Jesus' statement that the Father works "until now".
Isaiah 45:7 highlights that God creates both light and darkness and does all things, pointing to the Almighty Father's ongoing work of creation which Jesus refers to.

Hebrews 4:10-11 connects directly to this theme by showing that whoever has entered God's rest has ceased from their works just as God did at creation, yet Jesus confirms that the Father remains active in his work.
In John 9:4, Jesus repeats the same motif that he must work while it is day because the Father is working and he too is working, which is a direct theological parallel to chapter 5.
John 10:37-38 confirms that the Father's works are proof that Jesus was sent by him, and that the Father himself is in him and completes his work, supporting the claim made in 5:17.
